findings: The keeper's argument is correct as stated, checked against the library's openDiamond (Causal/Properties.lean:77, :80: openDiamond ⊤ p q = interior (J⁻_M(q) ∩ J⁺_M(p))). For N ∈ 𝓝 x and V = interior N, chronal neighbours give p, p' ∈ V ⊆ N with p ≪_V x ≪_V p'. The set I⁺_V(p) ∩ I⁻_V(p') is open in M, because the axioms isOpen_lt_right and isOpen_lt_left (Causal/Causality.lean:81, :83) are stated in M. It contains x, and it lies in J_M(p, p') by le_of_lt and le_mono (V ≤ ⊤). Causality.ChronalNeighbours.exists_lt_lt states exactly that; ChronalNeighbours.tarentin follows in three lines.
The edge is strict: the lightlike line is tarentin with empty chronology (label 2, lightlikeLine_separates_Z), and the ladder already records that pair (programme/ladder.toml:919-922).

source.statement: the dispatch: 'Prove the theorem with the weakest hypotheses that work'

hypotheses.note: to C.Zplus = univ ∧ C.Zminus = univ (def:strongly_tarentin_point, Causal/Properties.lean:137, :140). This is chronology in M at every point, inside each neighbourhood. Chronology in V enters the keeper's argument only to put p, p' in N, and lt_mono carries I⁺_V(p) ∩ I⁻_V(p') into I⁺_M(p) ∩ I⁻_M(p'). The weakening is strict: globalLine (≪ only in ℝ itself, Causal/ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean:346) has Z⁺ = Z⁻ = ℝ and no chronal neighbours. Under absolute minimality on a T1 space the two hypotheses coincide (Causal.Causality.AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalNeighbours_iff_Z, ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean:196), so the strictness holds only in the reading without gluing (globalLine is not absolutely minimal; kb/0014, OQ-18)

hypotheses.paper: is either hypothesis necessary for tarentin?
hypotheses.note: no: the lightlike line (GH, push-up, causally open, causally arc-connected, hence absolutely minimal) is tarentin while Z⁺ = Z⁻ = ∅ and it has no chronal neighbours. This holds in either reading

findings: For the author (no label marked, none touched): the step 'every point strongly tarentin in the future and in the past ⇒ tarentin' (Causal.Causality.tarentin_of_Zplus_Zminus, no separation axiom) is the abstract link between rem:lorentz_tarentin (ETT.tex:783-784) and the first claim of rem:tarentin_exemples (ETT.tex:689, 'Lorentzian manifolds are tarentin'). The paper gives the second remark without proof. The library has no Lorentzian manifold, so neither remark is formalised here.

The converse of that step fails in the paper's own models, by the paper's own statements (ETT.tex, not formalised here). A BTZ point is strongly tarentin in the future and not in the past (defi:causal_E0, ETT.tex:1349-1350), yet every E_{≥0}-manifold is tarentin (rem:sing_tarentin, ETT.tex:1364-1365). In Lean the lightlike line shows the same thing with no chronology at all.

readme_row: | `Causal.ChronalTarentin` | — | ETT programme, layer 1 (T-abs-chronal-neighbours-tarentin): chronal neighbours give tarentin with no separation axiom (`ChronalNeighbours.tarentin`); so does `Z⁺ = Z⁻ = M` (`tarentin_of_Zplus_Zminus`, via `Iplus_inter_Iminus_subset_openDiamond`), strictly weaker (`globalLine_separates_Z`); neither is necessary (`lightlikeLine_separates_Z`); the globally chronological line is tarentin and not absolutely minimal (`globalLine_separates_tarentin`); 2026-11-21 |
kb_proposals: 0076 (pattern) Two-sided chronology near a point gives tarentin there: the chronological diamond I⁺_U(p) ∩ I⁻_U(q) lies in the open diamond Int J_U(p, q) (Causal.Causality.Iplus_inter_Iminus_subset_openDiamond, from the openness axioms and le_of_lt). Hence Z⁺ = Z⁻ = M ⇒ tarentin and chronal_neighbours ⇒ tarentin, with no separation axiom (tarentin_of_Zplus_Zminus, ChronalNeighbours.tarentin). The chain chronal neighbours ⇒ Z⁺ = Z⁻ = M ⇒ tarentin is strict at both arrows: globalLine at the first (equality under absolute minimality on T1), the lightlike line at the second. To prove a model tarentin when it has chronology, show Z⁺ = Z⁻ = M instead of computing diamonds: globalLine_tarentin takes four lines (T-abs-chronal-neighbours-tarentin).
